source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:4 ('וחנך — this alone defective in the Torah, as I wrote in Pinchas')
claim_en: THE ONE LEAN ENOCH: וחנך ('and Hanoch,' the Midianite grandson of Keturah, 25:4) — UNIQUE and DEFECTIVE (no vav), while the name runs PLENE at every other bearer (builder-asserted): Cain's city-son (4:17), the walked-with-God patriarch (Gen 5, six tokens), Reuben's firstborn (46:9, Exod 6:14, Num 26:5) — twelve full Enochs and one lean Midianite.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:4 (the plene family, census frame)
claim_en: ...the plene family censused: bare חנוך eleven tokens, all with the vav.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:6 ('מתנת written defective — and our rabbis expounded in Sanhedrin, perek Chelek: he gave them a name of impurity')
claim_en: THE LEAN GIFTS: מתנת ('to the sons of the concubines Abraham gave GIFTS,' 25:6) — defective, no vav, and the Talmud's derash rides the lean word (the impure name handed east); the form stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — here and at the priestly forehead-plate atoning for 'the GIFTS of their holy things' (Exod 28:38): the concubines' gifts and the sanctuary's, one written form, lean both times.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:6 (Bereshit Rabbah 61 + Rashi read פילגשם lean — 'one concubine, Hagar is Keturah'; the Chizkuni and the Michlol against them: 'plene in all the precise books'; Minchat Shai concurs plene)
claim_en: THE CONCUBINES-WORD ARBITRATED: הפילגשים ('the sons of THE CONCUBINES') — the midrash and Rashi build the one-concubine reading (Hagar is Keturah) on a defective ktiv; the Chizkuni protests 'plene in all the precise books,' and SNAPSHOT agrees: the yod STANDS. The codex line arbitrates for the precise books; the one-concubine reading survives named-only, off the letter.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:13 (the Ramah: 'בשמתם defective — and every names-of-them in the Torah likewise; the printed Masorah's THREE is an error, for they are many')
claim_en: בשמתם ('these are the names of Ishmael's sons, BY THEIR NAMES') — defective, no vav, per the Ramah's whole-Torah rule that overrules the printed Masorah's too-small count.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:13 ('לתולדתם — first vav plene, second defective, in all precise books, the Hilleli, the Ramah')
claim_en: ...and לתולדתם ('by their GENERATIONS') — first vav full, second lean, exactly as all the precise books rule...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:13 (the Vaera Masorah: 'all the Torah's toledot so written, save TWO doubly-defective — the Levi list')
claim_en: ...and the rule's only exceptions censused whole: the DOUBLY-defective לתלדתם stands exactly twice — both in the Levi genealogy of Vaera (Exod 6:16, 6:19), precisely the Masorah's sign-verses.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:13 ('the zaqef qatan on נבית, and קדר with the lengthener — so in the precise books and in Chronicles')
claim_en: נבית ('Nevayot, Ishmael's firstborn') — under zaqef qatan (the small upright accent) as the precise books rule...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:13 (the Qedar leg)
claim_en: ...and וקדר ('and Qedar') carrying the lengthener-class stroke, matching the Chronicles mirror-list (I Chr 1:29; edge).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:14 ('ודומה — with the final heh, and plene; no heed to the Mikra Gedolah's emendation'; Or Torah and the Ramah concur)
claim_en: ודומה ('and Dumah') — final heh standing and the vav full, against the printed emendation, as the precise books and the Ramah rule. SNAPSHOT exact.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:15 ('חדד — with TWO dalets in all precise books'; the Chizkuni and the Ramah concur; the Masorah's pair in Chronicles; against Yonatan's sharp-blade rendering)
claim_en: חדד ('Chadad') — TWO dalets, unique in the Torah; the Masorah's pair is the Chronicles mirror (I Chr 1:30; edge) — the precise books' double-dalet against the Targum tradition that read a sharpened blade.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:3 ('ובני דדן — by the grammarians' rule the dalet should be dageshed; but in ALL the books rafeh, and rightly, per the Michlol')
claim_en: THE GRAMMARIANS OVERRULED AT DEDAN: the verse writes דדן twice — first (after 'and'-את, 25:3) with the dalet DAGESHED, then ובני דדן ('and the sons of Dedan') with the dalet SOFT after the vowel — the books and the Radak's Michlol against the grammarians' doubling rule. SNAPSHOT: soft exactly at the disputed site.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:3 ('אשורם plene vav, lean yod — all precise books and the Hilleli')
claim_en: אשורם ('Asshurim') — vav full, NO yod before the mem, as ruled...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:3 ('ולאמים lean vav, plene yod — in ALL precise books and the Hilleli; the Mikra Gedolah's ולאמם variant rejected; the Ramah: all bare לאמים likewise')
claim_en: ...and ולאמים ('and Leummim') — NO vav after the aleph, yod STANDING, exactly the ruling that rejected the printed variant.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:3 ('...and likewise ולטושם — plene vav, lean yod')
claim_en: DISCREPANCY: ולטושים ('and Letushim') — Minchat Shai's precise books rule it LEAN of yod like its neighbor Asshurim; SNAPSHOT writes the yod PLENE: the codex line splits from the ruling on the middle brother alone (the flanking two match). Watchlist — the counted-law-vs-codex class.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 25:9 ('החתי — in the precise Sephardic books NO galgal on the heh')
claim_en: החתי ('Ephron THE HITTITE,' at Abraham's burial) — the precise Sephardic books deny the galgal (the wheel-accent) on the heh, and SNAPSHOT stands with them: the heh carries the plain lengthener-stroke, no wheel. The galgal layer itself remains uninstrumented (standing gap: the stream encodes other marks where tradition names the wheel).

source: Bereshit Rabbah 61:3
claim_en: THE REMARRIAGE IS READ AS THE EVENING SOWING OF A FOUR-WAY PROVERB. A verse about sowing morning and evening is applied four ways - early and late crops, charity at both ends of the day, Torah in youth and in age, and students in youth and in age - the last carried with the account of twelve thousand pairs of students who died in one season because their eye was miserly toward one another, and a roster of survivors preserved in two conflicting versions. R. Dostai's application lands here: one who had children in youth takes a wife in old age, and Abraham at 25:1 is the proof.

check.note: A proverb applied four ways, landing on this verse, with a survivor roster preserved in two versions.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 61:4
claim_en: AN IDENTIFICATION CARRIED ON AN INK VARIANT OUR TREE DOES NOT HAVE. Rav holds the new wife is Hagar returned, against R. Nechemya's objections, each answered - the taking read as by divine command, the name read as PERFUMED with commandments and good deeds. The objection from the PLURAL 'concubines' at 25:6 is answered on ink: the chain reads the plural as written defectively, yielding ONE concubine, Hagar herself. Machine-checked against our corpus, our tree writes that word FULL and plural. The reading is recorded as the chain's own variant tradition and is NOT applied here; the identification stands or falls on its other legs.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 61:5; Onkelos Genesis 25:3
claim_en: THE DECLARED SHELF SPLITS THREE WAYS AT ONE VERSE, AND ONE MEMBER NAMES THE OTHER AS ITS OPPONENT. R. Shmuel bar Nachman states the dispute openly: ALTHOUGH THE ARAMAIC TRANSLATORS SAY merchants, iron-workers and heads of nations, they were ALL heads of nations - the midrash leg of the declared reading correcting the translation leg BY NAME, and ruling that the three names should not be translated as common nouns at all. And our own Onkelos renders them a THIRD way, as those who dwell in camps, in tents, and on islands. Three readings, two of them inside the declared shelf, with the disagreement explicit rather than reconstructed.

check.note: One member of the declared reading naming the other as its opponent, with the received text differing from both.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 61:6
claim_en: WHAT 'ALL THAT WAS HIS' MEANS IS A FOUR-WAY DISPUTE, RESOLVED BY DEFERRAL. R. Yehuda says the birthright; R. Nechemya the power to bless; the Rabbis burial rights and the testament, joining the will-document claim the machine records at gen_40; R. Chama says gifts and not blessings at all. The parable of two intertwined trees carries the last: bless one and the other rides in, bless neither and 'I have done my part, let the Owner of the orchard act'. The blessing is deferred to God rather than conferred.

check.note: A four-way dispute over an inheritance clause resolved by deferring the act rather than by deciding it.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 61:6
claim_en: THE DEFERRED BLESSING IS DELIVERED SIX VERSES LATER, INSIDE THIS SAME BLOCK. Having read 25:5 as a blessing withheld and handed to the Owner of the orchard, the chain closes the arc at 25:11 - after Abraham's death, GOD blessed Isaac his son. The parable is not left hanging: this block's own later verse discharges it, which makes 25:5 and 25:11 a matched pair rather than two independent notices.

check.note: A parable opened at one verse and explicitly discharged at another within the same block.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 62:3
claim_en: A PATTERN RULE FOR A FORMULA, WITH ITS BOUNDARY DEFENDED ON INK. R. Simon holds that wherever the full formula 'and it was after the death of' appears, the world regressed - four cases named: after Abraham the wells were sealed; after Moses the well, the clouds and the manna ceased; after Joshua the land's defenders were attacked; after Saul the Philistines warred. The counter-example is answered on ink rather than by exception: the passage that seems to break the rule LACKS the opening 'and it was', so the rule holds only for the complete formula. R. Yudan's mitigation is recorded - the world WOULD have regressed had successors not been raised. A canon-grade pattern rule that fires on our 25:11 and carries its own guard.

check.note: A formula-triggered pattern rule whose scope is defended by the presence or absence of one word.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 61:7
claim_en: THESE TWO VERSES ARE ARGUED IN A TRIBUNAL AS PROPERTY LAW. Gevia ben Kosem answers the Ishmaelites' birthright claim before Alexander directly from our text: Abraham gave ALL that he had to Isaac, and to the sons of the concubines he gave GIFTS and sent them away - a deed of gift plus severance, read as extinguishing any further claim. The narrative's disposition clause is used as an operative instrument in a live dispute, the counterpart of the standing-title doctrine the machine records at gen_39.

check.note: A narrative disposition clause deployed as operative property law in a recorded tribunal scene.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 62:2
claim_en: THE ORDER OF TWO NAMES AT THE BURIAL IS READ AS EVIDENCE OF REPENTANCE. That 25:9 lists Isaac before Ishmael is read as the maidservant's son according honour to the mistress's son, and thereby as the evidence cashing the claim, made at gen_40, that Ishmael repented in Abraham's lifetime. A leg left open in an earlier block is closed by the order of two words in this one.

check.note: Name order in a list read as evidence discharging a claim raised in an earlier block.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 62:2
claim_en: A REPAYMENT IS BOOKED ACROSS THIRTY-EIGHT YEARS. R. Tanchuma asks why 25:10 says Abraham was buried there AND Sarah his wife, decades after her burial, and answers that whoever showed kindness to Sarah merited showing it to Abraham - so the whole-city funeral recorded at gen_39 is receipted here. Shem and Ever are said to have walked before the bier and seen the plot reserved beside her, adding a placement detail to the cave's occupancy roster.

check.note: A kindness recorded in an earlier block explicitly receipted at a later verse; roster placement detail added.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 58:8
claim_en: THIS VERSE HOLDS THE NINTH OF THE TEN VENDOR-PARTY MENTIONS. The ten-fold census the chain reads against the Ten Commandments, machine-checked at gen_39, is not confined to that chapter: of its ten members, eight stand in Genesis 23, ONE stands here at 25:10 where Abraham is buried in the purchased field, and the tenth at 49:32 where Jacob names the same purchase. The census is a census of one conveyance, and this block carries a member of it.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 62:4; Megillah 17a
claim_en: A WICKED MAN'S YEARS ARE RECORDED IN ORDER TO DATE SOMEONE ELSE'S EVENT. Asked why the lineage and lifespan of Ishmael are written at all, R. Levi answers: to date Jacob's blessing. From the 137 years at our 25:17 the tradition computes that Jacob was 63 when he was blessed, the arithmetic carried in the Babylonian Talmud at Megillah 17a. The question itself - why record the wicked - is preserved with the answer, and a number in a genealogy is treated as a dating instrument for a scene in another block.

check.note: A genealogical number used as a chronological instrument for an event outside this block; arithmetic carried on the bridge shelf.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 45:9; Onkelos Genesis 25:18
claim_en: A POLARITY COMPLETED BY THE MIDRASH IS FLATTENED BY THE TRANSLATION. At 16:12 it was said he would DWELL among his brethren; here at 25:18 it says he FELL in the presence of his brethren. The chain reads the pair as a single rule with a hinge - while Abraham lived he dwelt, after his death he fell - so this verse completes a claim opened nine chapters earlier. Onkelos renders the same verb as SETTLED, erasing the contrast the chain depends on, and separately writes the standing geographic identification into the border name. One member sharpens exactly what the other smooths.

check.note: A two-verse polarity completed by one member of the shelf and neutralized by the other.
